**What this PR does / why we need it**:

using netlink instead of the conntrack binary removes
the external dependency in the conntrack binary.

I have a follow up PR to improve the conntrack e2e coverage

Signed-off-by: Antonio Ojea <antonio.ojea.garcia@gmail.com>

I've tried to add the new conntrack filter to the upstream netlink library
https://github.com/vishvananda/netlink/pull/544

so we can have a better control, in case we want to
fix or add new functionalities quickly.
Anyway, if the netlink library PR is accepted is straight forward to 
switch between one and the other.

> I don't completely object to this, if we think it's really a problem, but I do have one significant concern.
> 
> Specifically - e2e testing this is tricky at best. This is a fairly large amount of code to do something that we already have a thoroughly debugged tool to do. How can we get as much confidence in this as we have in `conntrack` ?
> 
> I didn't do a very complete review yet because I have no real context.

The context is that we found out that only one e2e test failed if the conntrack binary was not present in the host https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/91216#issuecomment-633710458 , and this test was added only some weeks ago. 

The other thing is that, when investigating some flakes, I realized that UDP service tests are generally more flaky than the others, the main differences with the other services tests AFAIK are that UDP is lossy and they kick the conntrack deletion, this is just a hunch, I do not have any evidence, maybe the system is dropping those packets under load 🤷 

Definitely e2e test is the key here, I'm working in another PR to implement e2e for those conntrack scenarios that must go before this PR, in order to compare `conntrack-tools` against this approach.

I'm not having a strong opinion on this, just wanted a quick feedback like the one you just gave and needed to verify that the change was feasible. 

If the risk is high and the benefit low, we can discard it.

Can we just featuregate this and use the old codepath / exec by default?

Would be curious to see the test results first of course.

I would definitely be AGAINST coding our own iptables lib.

This is somewhat less complicated, so I am not for sure against this, but
it seems that we need internalize details about netlink which increases our
cognitive burden.  The gain has to be worthwhile.

What is the alternative?  Fail harder in the absence of conntrack?

Yeah... I saw that `vishvananda/netlink` had some conntrack-related code and was hoping that we could use that to replace our calls to` /sbin/conntrack` they way we had previously (in openshift-sdn and ovn-kubernetes) replaced all of our calls to `/sbin/ip` with netlink calls, which made everything much cleaner. Maybe we should go back to that for now, and maybe also keep the idea of the `ConntrackClearer` abstraction from this PR (just still implemented using exec on the backend), and then if Antonio's netlink PR to add the filter code there gets accepted, we can think about porting `ConntrackCleaner` to use it later?

That sounds OK to me.  Making conntrack.Clearer or something seems like a
good standalone abstraction improvement

kube-proxy itself has already depended on conntrack being installed for a long time. I was assuming that the problem here was that the test case was invoking conntrack directly in some context other than where kube-proxy is running?
